insights.title: Thread one Hamiltonian line through the bipolar grid
insights.body: hamiltonian-path is tagged on 10 sketches, all square or polar lattices from nalee-one-line, while the bipolar (τ, σ) grid holds many walkers, never one. pen-stroke and bipolar-plot both landed. Run nalee-one-line's Warnsdorff walk over bipolar-plot's quadtree lattice, so a single unbroken meander packs every crescent cell from the frame's edge into both foci, and export it as one plotter path.

insights.title: Grow differential growth to pen width on an A4 sheet
insights.body: differential-growth is tagged on 2 sketches, both on screen, and its output is a single closed polyline, the plotter's native object; penplot holds 6 sketches. pen-stroke showed one long line on paper works. Run differential-growth's sim inside the A4 margin instead of a polyomino, set the repulsion radius to the pen's line width plus a gap, and keep growing until the curve has packed the whole sheet, then export one path.

insights.title: Run Gray-Scott on the GPU, one cell per pixel
insights.body: Reaction-diffusion is tagged on 2 of 412 sketches, and subtractive-diffusion runs it on a 100x100 grid of fat cells. physarum/gpu-million, the only webgpu sketch, already has the ping-pong compute passes and a three-stop ramp. Port subtractive-diffusion's Gray-Scott update into gpu-million's field pass at full canvas resolution, seed it everywhere, and let one coral or labyrinth regime cover the frame edge to edge, drawn through the same ramp.

insights.title: Fill an elliptic grid as the bipolar walkers did
insights.body: nalee/sketches/bipolar and bipolar-plot were both kept, and bipolar-plot was loved once its quadtree grid let walkers reach the foci. Conformal grids otherwise sit in 3 conformal-mapping sketches, only one of which (conformal-mapping/nalee) carries walkers, bent through sin(z) after the fill. Build the next coordinate grid natively, elliptic (μ, ν) coordinates about two foci, refine it toward the focal segment as bipolar-plot does, and let nalee walkers pack every cell.

insights.title: Pack noise streamlines at one even spacing
insights.body: flow-field is tagged on 36 sketches, and the curve-particles series seeds its trails at random, so they clump and leave holes. electric-field/hatch-field is the only sketch with a spatial hash, used to keep its seeds apart. Bring that hash to curve-particles' domain-warped noise as Jobard-Lefer evenly spaced streamlines: every line grows until it comes within one gap of another, then new seeds start on its flanks, until the whole frame is combed at one pitch.

insights.title: Run rival physarum species that shun each other
insights.body: physarum is 6 sketches plus terminal-ui/physarum-scopes, and two of them (gpu-million, physarum-scopes) were among the keepers of the last batch. Every one runs a single species: one trail map, one network. Give gpu-million three or four agent species, each following its own trail and repelled by the others', so the frame fills with interlocking networks that hold territory, one palette stop per species.

insights.title: Plot a physarum run as its agents' paths
insights.body: Only 6 of 412 sketches are penplot, all lattice drawings (heerich boxes, Hamiltonian lines, bipolar-plot), while physarum is tagged on 7 sketches that never left the screen. A slime-mould network is already a bundle of paths. Run physarum/basic past warm-up, record a few thousand agents' trajectories as polylines, simplify and clip them, and plot them in one fine pen, so the network draws itself in overlapping strokes across the A4 sheet.

insights.title: Sink a 64x64 maze into one stepwell terrain
insights.body: maze-distance holds 10 sketches, 9 made on 2024-01-09; the tenth, stepwell-voxels, was kept, and it extrudes a small maze whose few distance bands read as separate terraces. Heerich voxels already go to paper in panna-meena-p and nalee-p. Push stepwell-voxels to a 64x64 sidewinder maze so the distance bands become a fine continuous descent filling the frame, and export it as a heerich penplot like panna-meena-p.

insights.title: Settle a million grains on one Chladni plate
insights.body: The chladni technique appears on 5 sketches, and chladni/basic walks 10,000 particles onto the nodal lines, enough for a sketch of the figure but not its sand. gpu-million proved the WebGPU compute path for 2^20 agents. Move chladni/basic's amplitude-driven random walk into a compute pass with a million grains on a single high-mode plate (large m and n, so nodal lines cross the whole frame) and draw the settled density, not dots: a full field of sand.

insights.title: Fly a million boids and keep only their trail field
insights.body: Boids is tagged on 5 sketches, and the largest flock, boids/gradient-quadtree, holds 896 birds drawn as heads and gradient trails. physarum/gpu-million shows what a deposit field does at 2^20 agents. Run Reynolds flocking as a compute pass with a grid-binned neighbour search, drop the heads, and let each boid deposit into a decaying trail texture, so the flock reads as a combed, all-over current rather than a scatter of triangles.

insights.title: Let accretion clusters tile the frame until they meet
insights.body: cluster-growth has 6 sketches and its engine feeds 7, all from November 2024, and each stops short: one cluster from a seed, six on a dotted grid, or clusters capped by packed circles, with ground left between them. The accretion never ran to collision. Seed a few hundred clusters from cluster-growth/multi-random-static and let each spread until it hits a neighbour, so the shaded ascii blocks tile the whole grid as territories with no ground left.

insights.title: Fill the frame with a rug of soft bodies
insights.body: soft-body has 4 sketches, all from 2025-01-15, and stopped there; soft-body/rug already packed verlet rings into coloured blobs, and the other three are teaching and collision studies. Verlet physics is tagged on only 4 sketches. Scale soft-body/rug to hundreds of bodies under its quadtree collision and let them settle until every gap closes, so the Chaikin-smoothed blobs press into one edge-to-edge cellular rug.

insights.title: Stipple domain-warped noise with fifty thousand dots
insights.body: Weighted Voronoi stippling ran in 2 sketches in February 2024 (stippling is tagged 5 times) and stopped at 2,500 dots with their cells stroked. domain-warping is tagged on 21 sketches, and domain-warping itself gives a rich density field. Revive stipling-noise's Lloyd relaxation on that warped fBm with tens of thousands of points, drop the cell outlines and draw only dots sized by local weight, so tone comes from density alone.

insights.title: Spiral a cyclic cellular automaton across the grid
insights.body: cellular-automata is tagged on 19 sketches, but the 2D ones (test, grid-based-cellular-automaton) grow from one seed into a blob on an empty ground, and the 1D automata series stopped in January 2024. No sketch runs a multi-state rule from a random field. Seed every cell of grid-based-cellular-automaton's grid at random and run a cyclic automaton, each state eating the next, until rotating spirals fill the frame, one palette stop per state.

insights.title: Let the pipe boids pack the grid they walk
insights.body: boids/pipe is the one of 5 boids sketches that snaps headings to 45° and steps on a grid, which makes its trails nalee-like right-angled pipes, yet it wraps and overwrites instead of filling. random-walk is tagged on 28 sketches. Give each pipe boid an occupancy grid so it steers by flock rules but may not re-enter a claimed cell, and spawn new ones until no cell is free, so flocking writes the whole frame as one packed pipe field.

insights.title: Grow a DLA coral up from the whole bottom edge
insights.body: dla is tagged on 5 sketches: growth, growth-paths and growth-simple (all 2024-01-27) grow from one centre point, and isometric/landscape and stacks use it for cubes. Each growth sketch leaves a radial tree on an empty ground. Seed growth along the entire bottom edge and accrete until branches reach the top, so tapered gradient strokes cover the frame as a reef, then Atkinson-dither it as growth does, as the first of a series of seeded edges.

insights.title: Grow DLA coral in from every edge of the frame
insights.body: dla is tagged on 5 sketches, and growth, growth-paths and growth-simple all grow one tree from the centre to 1,400 nodes inside an 80% box, a specimen on a plate. Seed growth's nearest-node accretion along all four edges instead, raise the count by a hashed grid lookup, and keep adding until the branches from opposite sides interlock, then Atkinson-dither it as growth does, so the coral is the whole frame.

insights.title: Solve a maze too fine to see as a distance gradient
insights.body: maze-generation is tagged on 22 sketches and distance-field on 17, but maze-distance/basic stops at a 64x64 sidewinder drawn in distance bands, and stepwell-voxels landed by reading that field as height. Run the BFS on a maze with one cell every few pixels, map distance continuously through a long ramp and drop the walls, so the frame becomes one river-delta texture whose bands follow every corridor.

insights.title: Let a crowd of walkers claim every grid cell
insights.body: not-every-body-lives-the-same-way is a one-off from 2025-08-11 with no series, though random-walk is tagged on 28 sketches. Its walkers claim cells as solid, chequered and fives motifs, but the unclaimed cells are filled afterwards with hatching. Run it on a much finer grid with enough walkers that every cell is claimed by the walk itself, each walker keeping its own motif, so the frame becomes one dense quilt of claims.

insights.title: Let domain-skipper's one walker pack a fine partition
insights.body: grid-domain-nalee/domain-skipper is the only sketch in its series: one nalee walker fills a polygon-domain cell, backtracks and hops into the next until every cell is packed. The domain-polygon engine feeds 17 sketches, but subdivided grids fell from 34 sketches in 2025 to 2 in 2026. Rerun domain-skipper on a fine domain-polygon partition so the single walker's path covers the whole frame, each cell's packing a slightly different grain.
